title: Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2611.09701v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language-model systems can select prompts and parameter adapters repeatedly during deployment, using feedback to guide later choices. Earlier choices may change the context or environment inherited by later configurations. We study selection among preconstructed candidates and compare cumulative loss with the best fixed prompt--parameter pair used from the beginning. This excess loss separates into three terms: selection regret within the available family, the gap from restricting that family, and the benefit or harm of the actual deployment history. Selection is evaluated using the history each candidate would have produced if used throughout, which separates candidate quality from the effects of switching. When loss functions are fixed independently of selector randomness, past choices affect loss for only a bounded number of rounds, and every candidate's own-history loss is revealed, limiting switches yields sublinear expected regret

translated_title: 学习应该在哪里发生？文本、参数与联合自适应的遗憾分析
translated_abstract: 语言模型系统在部署过程中可以反复选择提示和参数适配器，并利用反馈来指导后续的选择。早期的选择可能会改变后续配置所继承的上下文或环境。我们研究了在预先构建的候选集合中进行选择的问题，并将累积损失与从头开始就一直使用最佳固定提示-参数对的情况进行比较。这一超额损失可以分解为三项：可用候选族内部的选择遗憾、因限制该候选族而产生的差距，以及实际部署历史所带来的收益或损害。评估选择时使用每个候选者若全程被使用时本会产生的历史，从而将候选者本身的质量与切换的影响分离开来。当损失函数独立于选择器的随机性而固定、过去的选择仅在有限轮数内影响损失、且每个候选者基于自身历史的损失都能被揭示时，限制切换次数可以获得次线性的期望遗憾。
tldr: 该论文将部署阶段对提示与参数适配器的重复选择形式化为在线学习问题，把超额损失分解为候选族内的选择遗憾、候选族限制差距和部署历史影响三部分，并证明在损失不受选择器随机性影响、历史影响有限且限制切换次数的条件下可实现次线性期望遗憾。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes repeated prompt and parameter-adapter selection during deployment as an online learning problem, decomposes the excess loss into selection regret within the candidate family, the family restriction gap, and deployment-history effects, and proves that limiting switches yields sublinear expected regret when losses are independent of selector randomness and past choices affect loss for only a bounded number of rounds.
